# Macros are not ambient: a macro resolves through an imported macro package,
# the same as any other qualified or dot-imported name. Nothing else covered
# this, so both halves could be reverted to the old ambient lookup with a green
# suite.

# A qualified macro needs its package imported.
! sngl check no_import.sngl
stderr 'unknown macro package "canvas": import it with import "internal://canvas"'

sngl check qualified.sngl
stdout 'qualified.sngl: ok'

# An unqualified macro resolves against dot-imported macro packages only.
! sngl check bare_builtin.sngl
stderr 'unknown macro "builtin": no dot-imported macro package declares it'

# `canvas` is a stdlib component as well as a macro package, so the default
# alias collides once the stdlib is dot-imported. An alias is the way out, and
# the diagnostic says so.
! sngl check collide.sngl
stderr 'import it under a different alias'

sngl check aliased.sngl
stdout 'aliased.sngl: ok'

-- no_import.sngl --
#[canvas.shape]
component blob(x int, y int) {}
-- qualified.sngl --
import "internal://canvas"

#[canvas.shape]
component blob(x int, y int) {}
-- bare_builtin.sngl --
#[builtin("int")]
struct Fake {
    v int
}
-- collide.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"
import "internal://canvas"

#[canvas.shape]
component blob(x int, y int) {}
-- aliased.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"
import cv "internal://canvas"

#[cv.shape]
component blob(x int, y int) {}

component main {
    text(value="x")
}
